subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Mutation Testing
description: A micro-lesson that makes Mutation Testing usable.

hook.text: Change a '+' to a '-' in the code. If no test fails, your tests are weak. That's the idea behind mutation testing.

buildup.text: Mutation testing introduces small deliberate changes (mutants) into the code to check if tests detect them.

discovery.text: If a test catches the mutant (fails), the mutant is 'killed.' If no test catches it, your tests have a gap.

twist.text: Mutation testing is computationally expensive. Thousands of mutants mean thousands of test suite runs.

climax.text: Tools like Stryker and PIT make mutation testing practical by optimizing which mutants to generate.

punchline.text: If your tests can't catch a tiny change, they can't catch real bugs.

quiz.question: What does mutation testing evaluate?
options: How well tests detect small deliberate code changes
